Wrote /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/coldstart_C05/partura/s805/r2/lit.md (106 lines), answering analysis.md §6's four literature questions (L1-L4), each tied to a core structure, each processing-method claim tagged [Sx] into a 19-row source table (all verified:true, with caveats noted inline where confirmation was secondhand or partial — e.g. S1's construction details came from cross-confirmed secondary summaries, not a readable primary PDF; S11 is an unpublished PhD thesis chapter, not peer-reviewed; S15's quantitative claims are abstract-only). Read PLAN.md §1-2 and the full r2/analysis.md first to get the exact core structures and pre-registered questions; checked partura/ops_ext.py for operator semantics (day_centroid, day_corr, in_index) to translate findings accurately into the project's operator language.

Key findings per topic:
- L1 (core 1, day_corr(Ret,Volume)): classic literature (Llorente-Michaely-Saar-Wang 2002, Karpoff 1987, Lin 2016, Chan-Fong 2000) works at daily frequency with regression coefficients or absolute-value correlations, not a rolling minute-level correlation; no paper found treating this exact statistic as a cross-sectional predictor; the smoothing-window question (needs >=20-day averaging) has no literature support either way.
- L2 (core 2, pairing day_centroid(Volume) with day_centroid(Ret)): Admati-Pfleiderer (1988) and Wood-McInish-Ord (1985) establish the mechanism/earliest evidence for the intraday U-shape; Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka (2010, verified by directly fetching the arXiv HTML and quoting its text) is the closest paper pairing volume and volatility intraday patterns, but only via linear regression control, which they show does NOT remove the cross-sectional effect — consistent with this round's own finding that linear subtraction underperforms nonlinear bucketing. No lead-lag (volume-leads-volatility) result found before the cutoff; the one paper that reports this (Örebro 2025) is excluded by date.
- L3 (§2.2's price/float-shares proxy): found literature split on whether nominal price is independent of size (Lu/Hwang thesis 2009 vs Elfakhani-Wei 2003's confounded-in-Canada finding) but found a directly actionable, A-share-specific treatment: Liu-Stambaugh-Yuan (2019, JFE) drop the bottom 30% by market cap as shell-contaminated rather than linearly controlling for it, and Lee-Qu-Shen (2017, Stanford WP) build a continuous "expected shell probability" variable instead — both map directly onto this round's R-item 13 (band variable swapped to market cap).
- L4 (§2.4's negative result, cross_zscore worst-in-table): turnover/cost erosion literature (Novy-Marx & Velikov 2016; Frazzini-Israel-Moskowitz 2012) and order-imbalance horizon-instability literature (Chordia-Subrahmanyam 2004; Chordia-Roll-Subrahmanyam 2005) are solid and applicable, but honestly reported: no literature was found explaining the specific mechanism (why a time-series standardized version of a persistent intraday-shape feature underperforms its multi-day average), and this round's result directly contradicts round 1's cited Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin / Lee-Kim-Kim literature (which found deviation-from-own-history superior) — flagged as an unresolved contradiction for the PI, with only an unverified mechanistic guess offered.

Also corrected two drafting errors before finalizing: a stray garbled character, and a mixed-up author attribution for the Weld et al. "Nominal Share Price Puzzle" paper (verified via direct WebFetch of the NBER page that WP 13762 belongs to Baker-Greenwood-Wurgler, not Weld et al., correcting an earlier search-engine conflation).
